title: Delivery view: next over a plan, milestone or task
summary: `@inventarch/runtime` exports next(handle, within, request?, options?), the delivery view of a plan, milestone or task (request.seat; omitted, the scope's only authored plan). It is computed on each read, stores nothing, makes every handle read through the scope token it is given and never reads the runtime band, and returns an immutable ia-next-1 view: the plan's milestones and each milestone's tasks in require order (a require cycle is a review item naming the plan's or milestone's owner, and no order is claimed), five state lines per record (accepted, admitted, realizable, realized, worked), each with its basis and read against the handle's retained snapshot when it retains one, each requirement's standing (a decision's choice, a predecessor's exit evidence, a spec's supersession as specStanding reads it, which keeps a partially superseded spec live for the scope it does not replace), one verdict per record (no declared blocker; blocked, naming its basis, a record another one supersedes included; or exit evidence recorded, naming the observation and its evaluator and whether it is self-attributed) and the ia position command for the first task with no declared blocker. Evidence comes through an EvidenceReader; the default, AUTHORED_EVIDENCE, reads authored observations only and names no overlay. A request it cannot answer is a DeliveryRefusal (IA-RUNTIME-REQUEST-INVALID) naming the command to run instead; a seat the scope does not read gets one refusal whether it lies outside the scope or names nothing. It is not a Door operation; the nine routes are unchanged.
